title: The role of serum adipokine levels in preeclampsia: a systematic review
author: Ioannis Bellos
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbipikdn
materials: Strategy for data synthesis A qualitative synthesis is planned to performed as the expected inter-study heterogeneity is high due to differentiations of laboratory assays across different settings. Moreover, adipokine serum levels often present skewed distributions; thus, precluding quantitative meta-analysis. The results will be summarized by tabulating the number of studies in which the examined adipokines are increased, decreased or unchanged in preeclamptic pregnancies. Furthermore, the quality of evidence regarding serum levels of various adipokines in preeclampsia will be presented.
Keywords adipokine preeclampsia leptin adiponectin resistin systematic review

steps.title: Perform Systematic Literature Search
steps.instruction: Search electronic databases and reference lists for studies investigating adipokine levels in preeclamptic versus healthy pregnant women.

substeps.instruction: Search MEDLINE, Scopus, CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Google Scholar from inception.
Perform a 'snowball method' search by reviewing the full reference lists of included studies.
Apply no date or language restrictions.

Use search terms: adipokine, leptin, adiponectin, resistin, visfatin, vaspin, omentin, chemerin, ghrelin, irisin, nesfatin, progranulin, retinol binding protein, rbp4, rbp-4, fatty acid binding, fabp4, fabp-4, fibroblast growth factor, fgf21, fgf-21, preeclampsia, pre-eclampsia.

steps.title: Screen and Select Studies
steps.instruction: Filter identified papers based on specific inclusion and exclusion criteria to select relevant observational studies.

substeps.instruction: Screen titles and abstracts of all electronic papers for potential eligibility.
Retrieve full-texts for all articles presumed to meet criteria.
Include observational studies (prospective/retrospective cohort, cross-sectional, nested case-control).
Exclude case-reports, small case series (<10 patients), letters to the editor, conference proceedings, animal studies, and review articles.
Ensure participants meet preeclampsia criteria: new-onset hypertension (SBP >140 mmHg and/or DBP >90 mmHg) after 20th gestational week with proteinuria or maternal end-organ dysfunction.
Ensure control group consists of normotensive women without proteinuria, edema, signs of maternal organ dysfunction, or pregnancy-related complications.
Exclude studies with gestational hypertension, no adipokine measurement, or no healthy pregnant control group.

steps.title: Extract Study Data
steps.instruction: Independently extract technical and clinical parameters from the selected studies.

substeps.instruction: Assign two authors to perform data extraction independently.
Resolve any discrepancies regarding article retrieval through consensus of all authors.

Extract the following parameters: first author name, publication year, exclusion criteria, study design, country, trimester of measurement, laboratory assay method, fasting state, maternal age, gestational age at sampling, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, and serum adipokine levels (leptin, adiponectin, visfatin, resistin, vaspin, omentin, irisin, ghrelin, nesfatin, chemerin, progranulin, retinol binding protein-4, fatty acid binding protein-4, fibroblast growth factor-21).

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias and Quality
steps.instruction: Evaluate the methodological quality and credibility of the included studies.

substeps.instruction: Use the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) score, evaluated by two authors independently with disagreements resolved by consensus.
For case-control studies, assess patient selection, comparability of cases and controls, ascertainment of exposure, and non-response rate.
For cohort studies, assess selection, comparability of exposed/non-exposed cohorts, outcome assessment, and follow-up period adequacy.
Evaluate evidence credibility using the GRADE framework (GRADE-CERQual tool) based on methodological limitations, coherence, data adequacy, and relevance.

steps.title: Perform Subgroup Analysis
steps.instruction: Conduct detailed analysis of adipokine levels based on specific clinical subsets.

substeps.instruction: Analyze by pregnancy trimester at sampling (1st, 2nd, and 3rd).
Analyze by preeclampsia severity (mild vs. severe, where severe is SBP >160 mmHg and/or DBP >110 mmHg or maternal organ dysfunction).
Analyze by preeclampsia onset (early vs. late, where early is before the 34th week of pregnancy).
Analyze by presence of obesity.
